observed.source: Codex session rollout (CLI-recorded thread settings; not model-authored)

result.decision_rationale: The focused gate passed on the requested commit. The toolbar implementation can still discard a player's move, restore a deliberately removed shortcut, leave duplicate bindings, or transfer a retired shortcut to a replacement companion. An existing combat regression assertion also passes on the base and fails on this candidate. The documented native playtest deferrals are acceptable under mission §7.

executed_verification: The controller receipt and matching log confirm that Test-Tiers.ps1 -Tier Fast -Focused Test-CityToolbarProneFocused.ps1 passed on 352c12aca79a1a681f75608a342fdf2edec7a1d8 in 47.2 seconds with the worktree unchanged. The transcript also confirms the guarded push of that commit.

The gate recorded 1,488 component checks, 153 source checks and 823 installed assembly-contract checks passing. All five new toolbar regressions passed. The contracts identified the installed IsBad, GetSlot and CleanupBadSlots methods and the native slot replacement instructions.

The focused wrapper passed all five children, including 21 click-composition checks across both patch orders, 9 archive checks and 22 six-pair adapter checks. The tested product DLL MVID was 2d7a5342-9cf7-4918-856f-d959a720c179.
The developer transcript records a separate pre-commit mutation run with 1,483 passes and five expected failures.

I evaluated the complete five-part target-liveness predicate from Test-Harness.ps1 against the command source at each revision. It returned true at dbf637021db42cdc9bf27f3d79fc255d4569c788 and false at the candidate.
inspected: The mission, AGENTS.md, validation policy, current handoffs, 32-file feature diff, developer report and tool transcript, focused receipt and log, and all five pending findings.
The native slot patches, placement intent, load fence, live reconciliation, archive capture and restore, and the component fixtures that model their ordering.
The capital roster adapter and projection, mounted stock attack admission and command lifecycle, compatibility checks, combat harness and owner playtest record.
limitations: The toolbar findings below are source traces. The component fixtures substitute native slot operations and reproduce parts of the service's control flow.
The area adapter produced the same 63 compiler diagnostics on the base and candidate. Its in-world restore assertion did not execute.

Native UI and combat checks remain deferred. The handoff identifies the missing candidate package, capital reader and fixture lineage, reserve-pet equipment driver, and enemy-posture setup. No native transaction ran, so restoration was inapplicable.
required_gaps: Focused regressions must cover edits to previously occupied copy indices, native cleanup of an occupied slot's fallback, exceptional exits, multiple cleanup reports for a retired rider, and bars with multiple canonical or legacy copies. Check the continuing bar and the cold-loaded archive.
The affected target-liveness assertion must pass while retaining coverage of native target legality and attack completion.
source_inspection_only: The two city issues have distinct mechanisms. Toolbar cleanup can discard a binding when its fact becomes unavailable. The capital's full-screen roster can list a reserve owner while its controllable-character filter omits that owner's pet.

The attack change carries an explicit player order on an already-unconscious living target through mounted admission. The conscious-prone path has a code trace. Actual firing, attack rolls and action expenditure remain unobserved on this candidate.

findings.actual: Entry.Copies still contains index 9 after its old binding is emptied. IsSecondaryBinding therefore classifies the new live binding at 9 as the old copy. Capture selects 3, and live reconciliation can clear the player's placement at 9.
findings.blocking_rationale: A deliberate move can be reversed in both the continuing game and the save.
findings.expected: The later player placement becomes the chosen slot. The continuing bar and archive each retain one shortcut at 9.
findings.requested_correction: Track whether the recorded copy still occupies the index. End its copy status when it is emptied, while preserving that status through a native rebind of the same copy.
findings.requested_evidence: Start with stale canonical bindings at 3 and 9. Empty both with GetSlot, place the current control at 9, then compare update-first and save-first results through cold reload. Retain the untouched-copy control.
findings.title: A new placement in a former copy's slot is discarded
findings.trigger: GetSlot empties the chosen shortcut at 3 and then its stale canonical copy at 9. Before reconciliation, the player drags the current control into the now-empty slot 9.

findings.actual: ObserveNativeSlotInvalidated rejects 9 because an interrupted choice exists at 4. This path never checks whether 4 is occupied. With both public bindings gone, reconciliation or capture gives up 4 and loses the shortcut entirely.
findings.blocking_rationale: Reading the fallback slot can erase the arrangement that the occupied-slot fix otherwise preserves.
findings.expected: Fireball stays at 4. The fallback at 9 remains recoverable for the same pet even when native UI empties its stale binding before KMC observes it.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the chosen-slot occupancy decision when processing native invalidation of the fallback. Preserve the fallback as interrupted when its former chosen slot has been taken.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend OccupiedChosenSlotWithCopy by calling GetSlot on stale alias 9 after placing Fireball at 4. Require one restored shortcut at 9, Fireball at 4, and the same result after save, reload and resave.
findings.title: Native cleanup can erase the fallback for an occupied chosen slot
findings.trigger: On the mixed older bar, GetSlot empties 4, the player puts Fireball there, and GetSlot empties the surviving stale alias at 9 before the next update or save header.

findings.actual: An exceptional exit leaves activeNativeSlotOperation set until Update. The standalone read on that bar passes the guard and queues a report. Update then attributes the player's empty slot to native cleanup and can restore it. The outcome classifier also treats an untouched stale slot as an emptying.
findings.blocking_rationale: The exception recovery path can undo the same deliberate removal that the normal-call fix protects.
findings.expected: A standalone validity read leaves intent untouched. Recovery records only replacements attributable to the native operation.
findings.requested_correction: Close or invalidate the observation scope at exceptional exit and distinguish an actual native write from an unchanged slot or later player edit.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise the production observation sequence with an aborted operation, a standalone IsBad read and a deliberate removal before Update. Require an empty slot and only the kind-7 placement marker after reload. Keep a completed native emptying as the recovery control.
findings.title: An aborted native operation leaves standalone reads inside its observation scope
findings.trigger: GetSlot or CleanupBadSlots throws on a rider's bar before its postfix. Before the next KMC update, a caller reads IsBad on a stale shortcut at 9 and the player clears it.

findings.actual: Both reports queue because each index is the first remaining canonical slot when native checks it. The first report retires A. The second finds no stored A identity to compare with B, calls ObserveBound, clears the retirement and remembers 9. Abandoning the load restores that choice for B.
findings.blocking_rationale: A replacement companion can inherit and persist the previous companion's shortcut.
findings.expected: Retiring A's arrangement invalidates the remaining reports for A's bindings from the same cleanup operation.
findings.requested_correction: Make retirement effective for all outstanding reports for that rider from the operation. Preserve later genuine placements and other riders' arrangements.
findings.requested_evidence: With autofill off, queue both canonical emptyings while the load fence is active, abandon the load, make B available and save. Require both old slots empty, no public binding row for B and an unrelated slot intact. Exercise the same batch outside the fence.
findings.title: A second cleanup report can reverse companion retirement
findings.trigger: A rider recorded with pet A now links to B. While a selected load fences the outgoing world, CleanupBadSlots empties stale canonical bindings at 3 and 9 with no active replacement fact.

findings.actual: ReconcilePublicControlSlots clears only boundIndex, the first surviving copy, then sets it to -1 and restores 3. Slot 9 remains callable. Recording 3 as live drops the remembered copy list, so later updates keep both shortcuts while the archive writes only 3.
findings.blocking_rationale: Live repair leaves a duplicate that can become the chosen shortcut after the player removes the restored one.
findings.expected: Recovery leaves one shortcut at 3 and agrees with the archived arrangement.
findings.requested_correction: Account for every surviving copy of the interrupted choice before restoring it. Preserve unrelated bindings and later player placements.
findings.requested_evidence: Use canonical bindings at 3, 7 and 9. Empty 3 with GetSlot and reconcile twice. Require exactly one shortcut at 3 before saving and after reload, then remove it and verify that removal persists.
findings.title: Repair clears only one of multiple surviving canonical copies
findings.trigger: GetSlot empties the chosen stale binding at 3 while two existing live canonical copies remain at 7 and 9.

findings.actual: The observer accepts the report for 9 but stores LegacyAliasIndex(slots), which is 4. ApplySlotInvalidation passes 4 to ObserveNativeAliasInvalidated. This marks the untouched shortcut at 4 as interrupted, allowing its subsequent deliberate removal to be undone.
findings.blocking_rationale: Inspecting a different legacy slot can resurrect a shortcut the player removed.
findings.expected: Only native invalidation of the selected binding itself can mark that binding interrupted.
findings.requested_correction: Match a legacy alias report to the actual selected slot before attributing an emptying to that choice, including in the outgoing load records.
findings.requested_evidence: With a valid selected Mount alias at 4 and a bad Dismount alias at 9, call GetSlot only on 9, then remove 4. Require a marker-only save and an empty bar after reload. Retain recovery when GetSlot actually empties 4.
findings.title: Emptying a secondary legacy alias is attributed to the selected alias
findings.trigger: An older bar has a recorded live Mount alias at 4, a bad Dismount alias at 9 and no canonical binding. GetSlot reads only 9 before the player removes 4.

findings.actual: Test-Harness.ps1 still requires the old inline IsFinallyDead expression. MountedPairAttackCommand now delegates that decision to TargetLifeAdmits. The complete assertion evaluates true on the base and false on this candidate.
findings.blocking_rationale: The attack change breaks an existing regression check for the exact combat path it modifies.
findings.expected: The harness recognizes the new explicit-order rule and continues checking in-state, hostility, CanAttack and native child completion.
findings.requested_correction: Update the assertion to cover the delegated life-state decision and preserve its other legality and completion checks.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the corrected affected check passing alongside the dead-target rejection and explicit-order downed-target controls. A focused reproduction is sufficient.
findings.title: The combat harness rejects the changed target-liveness implementation
findings.trigger: Evaluate the repository's existing target-liveness assertion against the candidate's MountedPairAttackCommand.cs.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: With chosen slot 4 free, the rebound legacy alias at 9 is recognized as secondary. The recorded regression checks one shortcut at 4 after reconciliation, in the save and after reload.
The untouched live-copy case passes. The manual-move control starts with 9 empty, so it misses reuse of a recorded copy's index after that copy was emptied.
Update-first and save-first agree while alias 9 survives until observation. Native invalidation of 9 before that observation still ignores the occupant at 4 and loses the fallback.
The new bracket protects standalone queries after normal returns. A missing postfix leaves that bracket active, and next-update recovery cannot distinguish a player removal from a native write.

The single-rebind case now clears A's slot. Production continues processing queued reports after retirement, allowing a second canonical report to recreate the choice. The batch fixture returns immediately on retirement.

summary.delivered_behavior: The candidate records per-rider toolbar choices using existing save rows, projects eligible owners' persistent pets into the capital roster, and carries a player's explicit order against an already-unconscious living enemy into the mounted attack command. The toolbar defects above prevent final readiness.
remaining_owner_review: After corrections, verify a moved or removed nondefault shortcut through capital travel, an interior transition and cold loads with two riders.
Select a reserve owner's pet through Inventory and Character, change permitted equipment, and verify the same pet and equipment after reopening and reloading.

Use the handoff's matched longbow cases in real time and turn-based mode. Observe actual rolls and action use against standing, conscious-prone and already-unconscious enemies at near and normal range, including the blocked-line-of-sight control.
summary.scope_reviewed: The complete final mission for draft PR #57, including the three reported behaviors, save and lifecycle compatibility, Tabletop Rules Expansion click composition, the focused gate and the five pending findings.
unresolved_questions: The owner's original weapon and target consciousness are unknown. A matched native observation is still needed to identify which firing stage accounts for the reported prone-target symptom.
